payload.author: framework-coordinator
evidence: The fresh scoped check names ?init@Flic@@QAEHPAUBuffer@@PADHHH@Z as the single unknown (expected-one-defined-function refusal) while all twelve protected byte obligations pass; the original image's own catalogue records the PAU spelling for init (src/flic.cpp:244 marker) alongside PAV spellings for Buffer::copy (src/buffer.cpp:1480, BYTE_EXACT), proving both keys coexisted in the original build. The MSVC mangler emits A for struct-keyed and B for class-keyed elaborated type specifiers at each declaration site.
payload.hypothesis: MSVC keys the A/B struct-class mangling distinction on the use-site elaborate-type-specifier, not on a translation-unit-wide class key: the original image holds ?init@Flic@@QAEHPAUBuffer@@ (struct-keyed parameter) and PAV-mangled Buffer::copy calls from the SAME original TU, which is only expressible when each declaration carries its own key. Therefore spelling init's parameter as 'struct Buffer *' in src/flic.cpp (declaration and definition, with buffer.h still included normally for the class-keyed copy calls) should emit the catalogued PAU symbol without touching src/buffer.h and without breaking copy linkage - unlike the measured full-TU 'struct Buffer;' forward, which rekeyed every use.
